title: Template: the trie walk
prompt: Complete the insert walk — this loop is the entire data structure.
explanation: Map the letter to a slot, create the child if missing, descend. Search is the same walk that returns null/false instead of creating.

title: Trie vs HashSet
prompt: You have 10⁵ words and must answer `startsWith(prefix)` queries. Why is a HashSet of words insufficient?
options: A set only matches whole words — checking a prefix would require scanning every word: O(n · len) per query
The set would use too much memory
explanation: Hashing is all-or-nothing. The trie shares prefixes structurally, so any prefix query is a single O(len) walk regardless of dictionary size.

title: Drill: minimal prefix tree
prompt: From memory: implement a `PrefixTree` supporting `insert(word)` and `startsWith(prefix)` (lowercase words). This is the core trie walk — insert creates missing children; startsWith follows them and returns whether the path exists.

solution.explanation: The class itself is the root node: `children[c - 'a']` is the next letter. insert creates missing children as it walks; startsWith follows the same path and fails at the first null. Both run in O(length) time, and insert allocates at most O(length) new nodes.

hints: Words that share a prefix should share a path. What does each node need so that you can step to the next letter?
Each node holds 26 child slots indexed by `c - 'a'`. insert walks the word, creating any missing child; startsWith walks the prefix without creating.
In startsWith: `if (node.children[i] == null) return false; node = node.children[i];`, then return true after the loop.

title: Template: wildcard trie search
prompt: Complete the DFS for a search where `.` matches any single letter.
explanation: Once every character has been matched, the match only counts if a word ends at this node (`node.isEnd`). A `.` tries each existing child with the next index and succeeds if any branch does; if none do, the result is `false`.
